items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: I told you, Dominic, you would have pirate on the ship.

ctx.x: It was only about six blocks from the place where I was playing, which was predominantly the Negro neighborhood. And they had this railroad track down there, as you recall, it was called Central Track. And that's where all the thugs lived. And I guess I was too younger to realize the danger. So he told me, you better get on home and get on home and run quickly, right quickly, because some of you niggas will take your head off. He thought I was a white boy. Yeah. So I said, okay, I thanked him so much, so I left…
How long has it been since you've been on a streetcar?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: And his daddy was the Dominic U, the captain of the fleet that Gene Lafitte was at the head of.

ctx.x: What about Dominic? We got a couple of minutes. You say you're some Ken to him?

I talked to one of my cousins yesterday. She's an old woman and way up in the 80s, close to 90. Her name is Lucia Goyns, G-O-I-N-S. And she was a Tomatis. And her mother was my grandfather's sister. My grandfather didn't have any brothers. He came from the Dominican Republic as far as we can be told by these older people that live in the country. And so very few of them that live in the actual history. And he had a sister but no other brothers. And his daddy was the Dominic U, the captain of the fleet that Gene…

You know, I've never understood, it brings me back to New Orleans, why somebody can be world famous and not make it in New Orleans, you know, musicians. It seems like they turn their back on me, this is off the subject.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: And I understand that his grandfather was Dominic Hugh, the pirate on the gene defense ship.

ctx.x: From what we understand and what we know from the Dominican Republic, derived the name Dominic Cutter-Hugh off of it. And I understand that his grandfather was Dominic Hugh, the pirate on the gene defense ship. Which is all authentic, because there's a lady died here just a few years ago. That was a close cousin, Miss Tomatis, and she told me about my grandfather's grandfather. How do you spell Tomatis? T-O-T-H-O-M-A-T-I-S.
I never heard of that name before. So they came up from the Dominican Republic?
